BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review of Seller update and disclosure letter

**Recommendation: reject the Seller’s package as drafted.** It weakens the agreed buyer risk allocation, leaves material completion risks unresolved, and treats several open matters as settled. In particular, do not accept the 20% general warranty cap or 18-month claims period: both require Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft, and none has been given.

The review below is based on the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA or underlying due diligence documents. The complete drafting and DD record should be checked before mark-up and Completion.

## 1. Liability, claims and disclosure

| Issue | Seller position and concern | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **General warranty cap — cl. 12.1** | 20% / **AUD 4.8 million**, below the buyer starting position. | Restore **25% / AUD 6 million**. The 20% fallback is unavailable without Amelia’s prior written authority identifying this draft. |
| **Thresholds — cl. 12.2** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket, with recovery only of the excess. Together, these materially reduce recovery for smaller and accumulated losses. | Require **AUD 5,000 de minimis** and **AUD 50,000 aggregate basket**, with liability **from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded**. |
| **General claims period — cls. 12.3 / 13** | 18 months, plus a proposed rule applying limitations to every claim unless expressly excluded. | Require **24 months after Completion**. Do not accept 18 months without Amelia’s written approval. Delete the blanket application rule or make each category’s treatment explicit. |
| **Fundamental/title claims** | Same cap and period as general warranties, purportedly for administrative simplicity. | Establish a **separate regime**: 100% cap, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. Include capacity and title protections. |
| **Fraud and misconduct — cls. 9.3, 12.8, 20.5** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims. This could undermine remedies even for serious misconduct. | Expressly carve **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** out of **all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is not waivable. |
| **Disclosure — Schedule 7 and letter [1.1]–[1.2]** | Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. The letter also makes no admission of liability or required action. | Reject blanket and deemed disclosure. Require **specific fair disclosure**, sufficiently identifying the matter and its relevance to the particular warranty. Assess the specific disclosures on their merits; the Seller’s reservation does not itself resolve the underlying risks. |
| **Buyer knowledge — cl. 8.3** | Bars claims based on actual knowledge of the Buyer or advisers and matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion, including the discoverability limb. Any negotiated knowledge qualifier must use **named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry**; it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. |
| **Category overrides — cl. 12.3 / Tax and IP** | The proposed all-claims limitation and assertion that Tax/IP are settled under the general regime risk silently overriding separately negotiated protections. | Keep **Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants** distinct, with express interaction rules and no hidden general-regime override. **Tax and IP terms remain open**; do not assume unlimited liability or an agreed resolution. |

## 2. Material transaction and due diligence issues

### Bluefen consent — completion condition

DD-002 identifies a material customer: approximately **AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue, or 30%**. The disclosure letter says no final written consent or evidence satisfying its associated conditions has been supplied. Reasonable endeavours and deeming the condition satisfied merely upon delivery of a consent do not adequately protect the Buyer.

**Push back:** make Completion conditional on **effective Bluefen consent and evidence that its conditions have been satisfied before Completion**. Review clauses 11.2–11.3 and the actual consent for continuing conditions, limitations and effectiveness. Do not treat this as cleared on the current record.

### Riverlark debt and security — completion funds flow

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** remains outstanding; no repayment or final security discharge is included. A release after Completion is inconsistent with the intended debt-free/cash-free acquisition and leaves the Buyer with security risk.

**Push back:** obtain a **current payout figure**, provide for **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and require effective security releases. A post-Completion release is a fallback only with an **irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval**. Reconcile the payout with the price and funds flow without assuming the approximate amount is final.

### Employee completion bonuses

DD-005 records **AUD 420,000** of conditional bonuses, omitted from the draft funds flow. Their conditions and any payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs need confirmation. Calling them “a matter for the Seller” without reflecting funding leaves an exposure gap.

**Push back:** include the bonuses **and triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or make them seller-funded**, with the payment and funding mechanics explicit. Verify eligibility, timing and applicable on-costs; do not silently exclude them.

### Ironquay IP — broaden indemnity and cure

DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, but this is not independent bank verification of non-payment; there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. A payment-only indemnity may not cover the resulting ownership, use or third-party claim risks.

**Push back:** broaden the specific indemnity to address losses arising from the Ironquay matter, including challenged or incomplete rights in the relevant materials, while **preserving the SOW3 cure**. Obtain independent payment evidence and an effective confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory title documentation. Do not assert either that AUD 180,000 is unpaid or that it has been paid without verification.

### Export/privacy incident — preserve and investigate

DD-006 records a link sent to an unintended external address; the export may contain approximately **1,240 records**. Access, exact scope and notification requirements are unknown. The Seller’s expectation of immateriality is not a substitute for investigation, but the record does **not** establish a breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount.

**Push back:** require preservation of relevant logs and evidence, a prompt investigation into access and scope, and continuing updates and cooperation, including assessment of any notification or remediation obligations as facts develop. Avoid asserting a confirmed breach or a numerical demand in either direction.

### Sandbar renewals

The three renewals total **AUD 330,000**. DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together; the disclosure does not establish whether the costs are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Neither the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation nor an automatic price deduction is justified on this record.

**Push back:** verify timing, scope, termination rights and accrual against the agreed price mechanics. **Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct AUD 330,000**.

### Title and authority

DD-012 is a company share register recording the Seller as holder of 100%; it is a supplied internal source, **not independent proof** of ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.

**Push back:** obtain independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence and reconcile it with DD-012. Retain the separate fundamental/title protections above; the register and disclosure are not substitutes for them.

### Office lease and Mossvale

- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a **notification obligation**, not a landlord consent requirement for the share sale. Confirm timing, responsibility and evidence of any required notice; do not invent a consent condition.
- **Mossvale:** DD-009 restricts **assignment**, but does not say consent is required merely because shares are sold. Review the transaction steps and contract before concluding consent is needed.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Reject the liability package:** restore the 25% general cap, AUD 5,000/AUD 50,000 first-dollar thresholds and 24-month period; establish the separate fundamental/title regime and mandatory misconduct carve-outs.
2. **Remove blanket disclosure and knowledge bars**, and prevent the general regime from overriding separate claim categories. Keep Tax and IP open.
3. **Make Bluefen effective consent and satisfaction of its conditions a pre-Completion requirement.**
4. **Fix the closing mechanics:** current Riverlark payout, direct repayment and effective releases; explicitly fund the bonuses and triggered on-costs.
5. **Address the remaining DD risks proportionately:** broaden and cure Ironquay; preserve evidence and investigate DD-006; assess Sandbar without automatic deduction; obtain independent title evidence; and verify the lease and Mossvale obligations without assuming extra consents.
6. **Escalate any proposed fallback to Amelia before agreement.** No authority has been given for the 20% cap or 18-month period; a post-Completion Riverlark release also requires her approval and an irrevocable undertaking.
